member.name: T:Spillgate.Brotli.BrotliCodec
member.summary: The brotli codec (RFC 7932) on the decoder of the .NET runtime (System.IO.Compression.BrotliDecoder), with Spillgate's own framing: the window is read from the first byte and checked against the cap before any decoding (SG-R-CDC-04, large-window streams are ), the input is handed over in exact steps so consumption is counted where the decoder takes bytes, and bytes after the last meta-block are corrupt. The decoder of the runtime is native code; docs/threat-model.md names the patch level it needs.

member.name: F:Spillgate.Brotli.BrotliCodec.Adapter.Step
member.summary: The decoder gets its input in steps of exactly this many bytes (plus the end of the input and the MaxInput boundary). The native decoder flushes output when it runs out of input and loses what it decoded in a call that fails, so how the stream is cut into calls decides which bytes are delivered before an error. Cutting it at fixed offsets makes the result independent of the source's chunking (SG-I-09).
